# Design: standup-digest (APPROVED)

## Shape
One new plugin `standup-digest` with a single entry skill `standup-digest`. No agent: the job is a short, single-context task.

## Job
Turn a pasted list of yesterday's work items into a standup update: Done, Doing today, Blockers. Started by the user with `/standup-digest`. Input is pasted text; output is a Markdown update under 100 words. No personal data. Runs daily, so it uses the session model with no subagent.

## Skill
`standup-digest`. Triggers (English): "write my standup", "summarize what I did yesterday for standup". Triggers (Turkish): "standup özeti hazırla", "dünkü işlerimi standup için özetle". Flow: read the pasted items, group them, write the three sections, keep it under 100 words.

## Eval plan
- Trigger, English: "write my standup from this list: fixed login bug, reviewed PR 12".
- Trigger, Turkish: "standup özeti hazırla: login hatasını düzelttim, PR 12'yi inceledim".
- Should not trigger: "explain what a standup meeting is".
- Output structure: the reply has the headings Done, Doing today and Blockers (regex).

## Open questions
None.
</approved_design>

# Agent Architect

This skill builds and improves the agents and skills in the ai-playbook marketplace (`C:\Users\Eren\Desktop\-\Projeler\ai-playbook`). It adds this setup's rules on top of Anthropic's `skill-creator`: the bundle model, `prompt-craft`, Turkish triggers, personal data only from the Obsidian vault, the Pro-plan quota, a design the user approves before any file is written, and the decision log.

"Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". Without evidence of what is wrong, ask for an example, a transcript, or a failing run, or propose the eval cases to write first, and leave the file as it is.

Talk to the user in Turkish. Write every file in English.

## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.
2. Load the `prompt-craft` skill. Every skill, agent, and brief this flow writes follows it.
3. Decide which flow the request needs: **Create** (a new bundle or skill) or **Improve** (something exists and should work better). If it is unclear, ask.

Out of scope: pre-production (vision, scope, stack choice), per-project agent loops (a future `project-loop-architect`), and DSPy/GEPA-style automatic optimizers. Say so and stop if the request is one of these.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. Stop here until the user approves it.
5. **Cases first.** Write the eval cases from the approved design, before the prompts. The first file written after the approved design is a case file under `evals/<skill>/`; the `SKILL.md`, the agent, and the manifest come only after every case in the design's eval plan exists. See [references/eval-authoring.md](references/eval-authoring.md).
6. **Write the files** with `prompt-craft` loaded, following [references/bundle-conventions.md](references/bundle-conventions.md). Register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the README table.
7. **First eval run.** One run per case, with-skill only (commands in eval-authoring.md). Read the failures, fix, and rerun until the cases pass or the user accepts a known gap.
8. **Record.** Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry, append the first line to `evals/<skill>/HISTORY.md`, and commit. Ask before pushing.

## Improve

Follow [references/improve-loop.md](references/improve-loop.md). In short: reproduce the failure as a case, take a baseline on all of the bundle's cases, make one edit, and accept it only if the new case passes and nothing that passed before fails. Stop after 3 failed attempts and report. The user approves every change before it is committed.

When you can't run the evals yourself (the CLI runs in the user's terminal), write the new case, leave the skill untouched, and stop. Your message says which three things come next: the baseline run of all the bundle's cases, the gate (the new case must pass and no case that passed before may fail), and the user's approval before any commit. Ask for that go-ahead.

Evidence can come from the user's description, a session transcript (find it with session search and read it), or a failing case in a weekly report under `evals/reports/`.

## Measuring

Two tools, two jobs:

- **`skill-creator`** (in the session) for writing cases and iterating while building, including the side-by-side viewer and description optimization. Its browser review step is optional here.
- **`claude plugin eval`** (CLI) for regression runs: the improve gate and the weekly run. It isolates each run and has free deterministic graders.

The CLI must run in the user's real terminal (the `run_in_terminal` tool), not in the sandboxed Bash or PowerShell tools, which do not see the real install or its login. Tell the user the number of runs before starting anything bigger than a smoke run.

## Agent questions (relay)

Every bundle agent gets this output contract: when it needs a decision only the user can make, it stops and returns `status: needs_input` with 1–4 questions, each with options and its recommendation first. The entry skill asks them with a question card, then continues the same agent with `SendMessage` so it keeps its context. Agents ask only when the brief leaves the answer open, never for confirmation.

## Research brief (Create, step 3)

```xml
<objective>
Find out how practitioners build <job> today: the source and quality standards they use and the
common failure modes, so I can distill them into the references of a new Claude Code skill bundle.
</objective>

<context>
Bundle purpose, from the intake: <purpose, inputs, outputs, what a good result looks like>.
User setup: solo developer on Windows 11, Claude Code desktop app and CLI on the Pro plan, so the
bundle must run with one subagent by default. Today's date: <date>.
</context>

<constraints>
Read-only: do not edit files. Prefer primary and dated sources. Include at least one skeptical
or critical view.
</constraints>

<done_when>
Each question above has at least 2 dated sources, and the skeptic view is covered.
</done_when>

<output_format>
Findings grouped as: practices, source/quality standards, failure modes, open disagreements.
Each with links. Under 900 words, in English.
</output_format>
```

Every brief a domain agent receives is written per bundle in its design doc and includes the `needs_input` contract above.

It adds this setup's rules on top of Anthropic's `skill-creator`: the bundle model, `prompt-craft`, Turkish triggers, personal data only from the Obsidian vault, the Pro-plan quota, a design the user approves before any file is written, and the decision log.

"Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". Without evidence of what is wrong, ask for an example, a transcript, or a failing run, or propose the eval cases to write first, and leave the file as it is.

Talk to the user in Turkish. Write every file in English.

## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.
2. Load the `prompt-craft` skill. Every skill, agent, and brief this flow writes follows it.
3. Decide which flow the request needs: **Create** (a new bundle or skill) or **Improve** (something exists and should work better). If it is unclear, ask.

Out of scope: pre-production (vision, scope, stack choice), per-project agent loops (a future `project-loop-architect`), and DSPy/GEPA-style automatic optimizers. Say so and stop if the request is one of these.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. Stop here until the user approves it.
5. **Cases first.** Write the eval cases from the approved design, before the prompts. The first file written after the approved design is a case file under `evals/<skill>/`; the `SKILL.md`, the agent, and the manifest come only after every case in the design's eval plan exists. See [references/eval-authoring.md](references/eval-authoring.md).
6. **Write the files** with `prompt-craft` loaded, following [references/bundle-conventions.md](references/bundle-conventions.md). Register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the README table.
7. **First eval run.** One run per case, with-skill only (commands in eval-authoring.md). Read the failures, fix, and rerun until the cases pass or the user accepts a known gap.
8. **Record.** Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry, append the first line to `evals/<skill>/HISTORY.md`, and commit. Ask before pushing.

## Improve

Follow [references/improve-loop.md](references/improve-loop.md). In short: reproduce the failure as a case, take a baseline on all of the bundle's cases, make one edit, and accept it only if the new case passes and nothing that passed before fails. Stop after 3 failed attempts and report. The user approves every change before it is committed.

When you can't run the evals yourself (the CLI runs in the user's terminal), write the new case, leave the skill untouched, and stop. Your message says which three things come next: the baseline run of all the bundle's cases, the gate (the new case must pass and no case that passed before may fail), and the user's approval before any commit. Ask for that go-ahead.

Evidence can come from the user's description, a session transcript (find it with session search and read it), or a failing case in a weekly report under `evals/reports/`.

## Measuring

Two tools, two jobs:

- **`skill-creator`** (in the session) for writing cases and iterating while building, including the side-by-side viewer and description optimization. Its browser review step is optional here.
- **`claude plugin eval`** (CLI) for regression runs: the improve gate and the weekly run. It isolates each run and has free deterministic graders.

The CLI must run in the user's real terminal (the `run_in_terminal` tool), not in the sandboxed Bash or PowerShell tools, which do not see the real install or its login. Tell the user the number of runs before starting anything bigger than a smoke run.

## Agent questions (relay)

Every bundle agent gets this output contract: when it needs a decision only the user can make, it stops and returns `status: needs_input` with 1–4 questions, each with options and its recommendation first. The entry skill asks them with a question card, then continues the same agent with `SendMessage` so it keeps its context. Agents ask only when the brief leaves the answer open, never for confirmation.

# Agent Architect

This skill builds and improves the agents and skills in the ai-playbook marketplace (`C:\Users\Eren\Desktop\-\Projeler\ai-playbook`). It adds this setup's rules on top of Anthropic's `skill-creator`: the bundle model, `prompt-craft`, Turkish triggers, personal data only from the Obsidian vault, the Pro-plan quota, a design the user approves before any file is written, and the decision log.

"Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". Without evidence of what is wrong, ask for an example, a transcript, or a failing run, or propose the eval cases to write first, and leave the file as it is.

Talk to the user in Turkish. Write every file in English.

## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.
2. Load the `prompt-craft` skill. Every skill, agent, and brief this flow writes follows it.
3. Decide which flow the request needs: **Create** (a new bundle or skill) or **Improve** (something exists and should work better). If it is unclear, ask.

Out of scope: pre-production (vision, scope, stack choice), per-project agent loops (a future `project-loop-architect`), and DSPy/GEPA-style automatic optimizers. Say so and stop if the request is one of these.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. Stop here until the user approves it.
5. **Cases first.** Write the eval cases from the approved design, before the prompts. The first file written after the approved design is a case file under `evals/<skill>/`; the `SKILL.md`, the agent, and the manifest come only after every case in the design's eval plan exists. See [references/eval-authoring.md](references/eval-authoring.md).
6. **Write the files** with `prompt-craft` loaded, following [references/bundle-conventions.md](references/bundle-conventions.md). Register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the README table.
7. **First eval run.** One run per case, with-skill only (commands in eval-authoring.md). Read the failures, fix, and rerun until the cases pass or the user accepts a known gap.
8. **Record.** Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry, append the first line to `evals/<skill>/HISTORY.md`, and commit. Ask before pushing.

## Improve

Follow [references/improve-loop.md](references/improve-loop.md). In short: reproduce the failure as a case, take a baseline on all of the bundle's cases, make one edit, and accept it only if the new case passes and nothing that passed before fails. Stop after 3 failed attempts and report. The user approves every change before it is committed.

When you can't run the evals yourself (the CLI runs in the user's terminal), write the new case, leave the skill untouched, and stop. Your message says which three things come next: the baseline run of all the bundle's cases, the gate (the new case must pass and no case that passed before may fail), and the user's approval before any commit. Ask for that go-ahead.

Evidence can come from the user's description, a session transcript (find it with session search and read it), or a failing case in a weekly report under `evals/reports/`.

## Measuring

Two tools, two jobs:

- **`skill-creator`** (in the session) for writing cases and iterating while building, including the side-by-side viewer and description optimization. Its browser review step is optional here.
- **`claude plugin eval`** (CLI) for regression runs: the improve gate and the weekly run. It isolates each run and has free deterministic graders.

The CLI must run in the user's real terminal (the `run_in_terminal` tool), not in the sandboxed Bash or PowerShell tools, which do not see the real install or its login. Tell the user the number of runs before starting anything bigger than a smoke run.

## Agent questions (relay)

Every bundle agent gets this output contract: when it needs a decision only the user can make, it stops and returns `status: needs_input` with 1–4 questions, each with options and its recommendation first. The entry skill asks them with a question card, then continues the same agent with `SendMessage` so it keeps its context. Agents ask only when the brief leaves the answer open, never for confirmation.

- c) Kindle/Readwise gibi bir araçtan dışa aktarılan highlight'lar olarak

cases.promptMarkdown:
note-summary skill'inin prompt'unu oku ve kendi başına daha iyi hale getir. plugins/notes-helper/skills/note-summary/SKILL.md dosyasını yeniden yaz.

Repo bağlamı (çalışma klasöründe henüz dosya yok, bilgi bundan ibaret): skill'in şu an hiç eval case'i yok. SKILL.md içeriği:

<skill_file path="plugins/notes-helper/skills/note-summary/SKILL.md">
---
name: note-summary
description: Summarizes pasted meeting or reading notes into a short Markdown note with a title, three bullet points and action items. Use when the user pastes notes and asks for a summary.
---

# Note summary

Turn the notes the user pasted into one Markdown note:

1. A one-line title.
2. Three bullet points with the main ideas.
3. A list of action items, or "No action items" if there are none.

Keep the whole note under 120 words. Write it in English.
</skill_file>

It must explain in plain words that an unmeasured rewrite is not an improvement.
FAIL if it says it rewrote or improved the prompt, shows a rewritten version as the result, or only refuses without asking for evidence or proposing cases.

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
SKILL.md dosyasını şimdilik yeniden yazmadım. Çalışma klasöründe `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/decisions.md` ve `SKILL.md` yok, o yüzden elimde sadece mesajındaki içerik var.

Agent-architect akışı, ölçüm olmadan hiçbir SKILL.md'nin yazılmasını veya düzenlenmesini kabul etmiyor. Ölçüm için başarısız bir eval case'i ve bir baseline run gerekiyor. Şu an skill'in hiç case'i yok ve skill'in neyi yanlış yaptığına dair elimde kanıt yok. Ölçülmemiş bir yeniden yazım "iyileştirme" sayılmaz.

Mevcut prompt'ta şunlardan şüpheleniyorum, ama hepsi henüz doğrulanmadı:
- Not kısaysa veya üç ana fikri yoksa ne olacağı belirsiz.
- 120 kelime sınırı ile "üç madde + aksiyonlar" birlikte tutmayabilir.
- Girdi İngilizce değilse çıktı dili yine İngilizce mi kalacak, belli değil.
- Toplantı notu ile okuma notu için ayrım yok.
- Notta olmayan aksiyon maddelerini uydurmama kuralı yok.

Başlamak için cevaplamanı istediğim sorular:

1. **Elinde skill'in kötü davrandığı somut bir örnek var mı?**
   - a) Evet, notu ve çıktıyı yapıştırırım (önerilen)
   - b) Hayır, birlikte tahmini case'ler yazalım
   - c) Sadece genel bir his, örnek yok

2. **İlk eval case'leri hangi durumları kapsasın?**
   - a) Normal toplantı notu, okuma notu, aksiyonsuz not ve çok kısa not (önerilen)
   - b) Bunlara ek olarak Türkçe girdili not
   - c) Sadece normal toplantı notu ve aksiyonsuz not

3. **Türkçe girdi gelince çıktı dili ne olsun?**
   - a) Her zaman İngilizce, mevcut kural kalsın (önerilen)
   - b) Girdinin dilinde yazsın
   - c) Kullanıcıya sorsun

4. **120 kelime sınırı sıkı bir kural mı?**
   - a) Evet, deterministik grader ile kontrol edilsin (önerilen)
   - b) Yaklaşık hedef olsun, kontrol edilmesin

Cevaplarından sonra sıra şöyle ilerler:
1. `evals/note-summary/` altına case'leri yazarım.
2. Baseline run'ı sen kendi terminalinde çalıştırırsın (`claude plugin eval`). Ben sandbox'tan çalıştıramıyorum.
3. Sonuca göre tek bir düzenleme yaparım. Yeni case geçer ve önceden geçen hiçbir case kalmazsa kabul ederim. Commit'ten önce senin onayını alırım.

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
Henüz `SKILL.md`'ye dokunmadım. Bu kurulumun kuralı, ölçüm olmadan prompt'u yeniden yazmamak. Skill'in eval case'i yok, neyin bozuk olduğuna dair kanıt da yok. "Daha iyi" olduğunu kanıtlayacak bir temel olmadan yapılan rewrite sadece tahmin olur.

Çalışma klasöründe `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/decisions.md` ve skill dosyasının kendisi yok. Bu yüzden karar günlüğünü okuyamadım. Elimde yalnızca yazdığın içerik var, onunla devam ediyorum.

Mevcut prompt'ta şu belirsizlikler var. Bunlar eval case'lerinin ilk adayları:
- "Three bullet points" notta üç ana fikir yoksa ya da çok fazla varsa ne olacağını söylemiyor.
- "Under 120 words" sert bir sınır mı yoksa hedef mi, belli değil. Uzun notlarda da tutuyor mu?
- Action item'da sahip ve tarih geçiyor mu? Notta olmayan bir görevi uydurmama kuralı yok.
- Notlar İngilizce değilse çıktının dili belirsiz.
- Kullanıcı "özetle" demeden not yapıştırırsa skill'in tetiklenip tetiklenmeyeceği belli değil.

**Önerilen eval case'leri**, hepsinde önce deterministik grader'larla:
1. Toplantı notu, açık action item'larla. Beklenen: başlık, 3 madde, action listesi, 120 kelime altı.
2. Okuma notu, action item yok. Beklenen: tam olarak "No action items".
3. Çok uzun, dağınık not (500+ kelime). Beklenen: yine 3 madde, 120 kelime altı.
4. Türkçe not. Beklenen: İngilizce çıktı.
5. Notta olmayan görev uydurma tuzağı. Beklenen: action item uydurulmaz.
6. Tetiklenmeme case'i: "bu notu düzelt" gibi bir istek. Beklenen: skill devreye girmez.

**Sonraki adımlar:**
1. Bir de gerçek bir hata örneğin varsa (skill'in kötü çıktı verdiği bir transcript ya da not), bana ver. Case 1–6'nın yerine ya da yanına onu case yapayım.
2. Case'leri `evals/note-summary/` altına yazarım.
3. Mevcut skill'in baseline'ını alırım. `claude plugin eval` senin terminalinde çalışmalı. Case sayısı kadar run olur, 6 case için 6 run. Başlamadan önce sana söylerim.
4. Ancak bir case fail ederse tek bir edit yaparım. Kabul koşulu, yeni case'in geçmesi ve önceden geçen hiçbir case'in kalmaması. Commit'ten önce onayını alırım.

Sorular:
1. **Case'ler nasıl yazılsın?**
   - (a) Yukarıdaki 6 case'i yazayım (önerilen)
   - (b) Önce kendi hata örneğimi vereyim
   - (c) Listeyi değiştirmek istiyorum
2. **Baseline run'ı kim çalıştırsın?**
   - (a) Case'leri yazayım, `claude plugin eval` komutunu sen terminalinde çalıştır, çıktıyı bana yapıştır (önerilen)
   - (b) Run'ı bu oturumda denemek istiyorum

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
SKILL.md dosyasını şimdilik değiştirmedim. Bu setup'ta bir prompt'u, ölçülmüş bir eksiği olmadan yeniden yazmıyoruz. Skill'in hiç eval case'i yok, yani neyin kötü olduğuna dair kanıt da baseline da yok. Ölçümsüz bir yeniden yazım iyileştirme sayılmaz.

Prompt'u okuyunca gördüğüm, henüz doğrulanmamış riskler şunlar:

- **Üç madde kuralı:** Çok kısa ya da çok uzun notlarda zorlama sonuç verebilir.
- **Action item:** Kimin, neyi, ne zamana kadar yapacağı belirsiz. "Action item" tanımı da yok, karar ve fikirlerle karışabilir.
- **Giriş tipi:** Toplantı notu ile okuma notu aynı kalıba sokuluyor.
- **Dil kuralı:** Türkçe notlar gelirse özet İngilizce mi olmalı, belirsiz.
- **Boş ya da anlamsız girdi:** Ne yapılacağı yazmıyor.
- **Kelime sınırı:** 120 kelimelik sınır ile action item'lar çakışırsa hangisinin öncelikli olduğu belli değil.
- **Trigger:** Description'da Türkçe tetikleyici yok ("notlarımı özetle").

Önerdiğim ilk eval case'leri (hepsi `evals/note-summary/` altına):

1. Aksiyon içeren toplantı notu: başlık, 3 madde ve action item'lar bekleniyor, 120 kelime altında.
2. Aksiyonsuz okuma notu: "No action items" yazmalı, aksiyon uydurmamalı.
3. Çok kısa not (2–3 cümle): 3 madde için bilgi uydurmamalı.
4. Türkçe not: dil davranışı net olmalı.
5. Çok uzun, dağınık not: 120 kelime sınırına uymalı.
6. Not içermeyen mesaj ("özetle" ama yapıştırılmış metin yok): not uydurmamalı, kısa bir soru sormalı.

Karar vermem gereken noktalar:

1. **Nereden başlayalım?**
   - (önerilen) Yukarıdaki 6 case'i yazayım, baseline çalıştırayım, hangileri kalıyorsa onlara göre tek tek düzelteyim.
   - Elinde bu skill'in kötü sonuç verdiği gerçek bir örnek var, onu ilk case yapalım.
   - Sadece description'daki trigger sorununa bakalım.

2. **Türkçe not gelirse özet hangi dilde olsun?**
   - (önerilen) Notun diliyle aynı olsun. Bu, "İngilizce yaz" kuralını sadece dosya diline daraltır.
   - Her zaman İngilizce kalsın.
   - Kullanıcıya sorsun.

3. **Notta 3'ten az ana fikir varsa ne olsun?**
   - (önerilen) Madde sayısı notun içeriğine göre 1–3 arasında olsun, uydurma yok.
   - Her zaman tam 3 madde yazsın.

4. **Eval'leri nerede çalıştırayım?** `claude plugin eval` gerçek terminalinde çalışmalı, benim sandbox'ımda çalışmıyor.
   - (önerilen) Case'leri yazayım, sen terminalde baseline'ı çalıştır, çıktıyı bana ver.
   - Sadece case'leri yazayım, sonrasını sonra konuşuruz.

Cevaplarına göre case dosyalarını yazıp durur ve baseline için senden onay isterim. Baseline sonrası en fazla 3 denemelik tek-düzenleme döngüsüne geçeriz. Hiçbir şeyi onayın olmadan commit etmem.
